chapter_theme: Three songs at Nagapattinam (நாகப்பட்டினம்): the poet repents of praising dull men as famous and the base as lords; he will not forget the feet even while he wanders in desire; and he asks for an unfailing boon against a life wasted in materialism and infatuation.
structure_note: 828 repents of patron praise; 829 is a catalogue of women's bodies ending in a vow not to forget the feet; 830 names Lokayata.

828.reading: The poet confesses that, asking who in this sea-girt world equals the clouds and the kalpaka trees, he called the dumb famous, fools capable and base men lords, composed fine Tamil prabandhas for them, spoke countless wants and wandered in vain like a dog; he asks when, with anger and delusion gone, Murugan will give him liberation, to worship him and join him. The praise names the Mother, Durga, Shakti, Ambika, who is in the half of the mad Lord and bore him, the vel thrown at Krauncha, Narayana who swallowed the world and sleeps on the serpent as uncle, and the slayer of Surapadma at Nagapattinam.
828.nuance: ஊமரைப் பிரசித்தர் என்றும் மூடரைச் சமர்த்தர் என்றும் ஊனரைப் பிரபுக்கள் என்றும்: the inversions of patron poetry are listed plainly. முகில் தருக்கள் ஒன்றும் அவர் ஆர்: the patron is flattered as cloud and kalpaka tree, the same flattery quoted in 827.

829.reading: The poet lists, part by part, the bodies of dancing young women: breasts like hills with necklaces and garlands, sword-like eyes, swinging earrings and heavy hair, moon faces and lotus lips, conch throats, turmeric arms, nails like parrots' beaks, a thin waist, the 'vessel of pleasure', banana thighs, anklets and bells, and says that even if he wanders thirsting for union with them he will not forget the feet where the anklets ring. The praise has drums and conches sound as Sura's pride is ended and the many-hooded serpent's peak struck while the vel dances, names Vishnu who as Narasimha made Hiranya tremble and with the bow ended Ravana's clan, the hunter girl, the nectar-formed maiden of knowledge, 'my one mother', and the lord at Nagai praised by devotees.
829.nuance: The plea is concessive: கலவி தாகம் உண்டு உழல்கினும் கழல் உறும் கழல் மறந்திடேனே, even while wandering in desire, the poet will not forget the feet. Valli is called என்றன் ஒரு தாய், 'my one mother'. Line 21 ends in a garble (தந்த்முல), which leaves the lines on Valli uncertain.

830.reading: The poet asks that, rather than let his days pass in waste, not thinking the body will fall, doing only what binds deeds, with Lokayata in the ascendant and weeping and ruined by infatuation with women, he be given an undying boon: to praise Murugan and be joined as kin to his flower feet. The praise names the god who uproots the deeds of those who worship and gives the stainless supreme, king of the gods, abode of compassion, life of devotees, the end of the unwritten Veda, the Lord who rules the poet, and asks him to give whatever is to be given, even himself, at Nagai.
830.nuance: உலகாயதம் மேலிடவே: the poet names Lokayata, the materialist school that denies anything beyond the body, as part of his wasted life. எழுதா மறை, 'the unwritten Veda', is the oral scripture. இறைவா எது தாவது அது தா தனையே is open; it may ask the Lord to give himself.

links.note: Both repent of patron praise: 827 quotes the flattery, calling a miser the kalpaka tree that protects poets, and 828 lists its inversions, the dumb called famous, fools capable and the base lords, with the patron set beside cloud and kalpaka tree.

828 repents of calling fools capable and base men lords (மூடரைச் சமர்த்தர் என்றும் ஊனரைப் பிரபுக்கள் என்றும்) in fine Tamil poems out of countless wants, and asks to worship Murugan instead. Tirumanthiram 269 says not to wither praising petty-minded men for their wealth (புல்லறிவாளரைப் போற்றிப் புலராமல்) but to praise the Lord. The Tirumanthiram's command is the song's repentance, with the same turn from patron to God.

829 says that even if he wanders thirsting for union with dancing women (கலவி தாகம் உண்டு உழல்கினும்) he will not forget the feet. Naladiyar 378 says those who mean to reach the right path will not embrace such women's breasts (தடமுலை சேராரே செந்நெறிச் சேர்துமென் பார்). On the reading that 829 lets desire and devotion run together, the two disagree about whether the path survives the embrace.

830 confesses not thinking the body will fall (விழுதாது எனவே கருதாது உடலை) while Lokayata ruled his mind, and asks for an undying boon. Tirumanthiram 312 addresses those who feel this perishing hut is permanent (நில்லாக் குரம்பை நிலையென்று உணர்வீர்காள்) and says the Lord is not seen in such hearts. Both name the mistake of taking the body as lasting; the song ties it to the materialist school by name.
